descriptionChirho: Noun denoting something extraordinary, a wonder or marvel, typically referring to God's miraculous and awe-inspiring acts. Used of YHWH's mighty deeds in salvation history (Ex 15:11 'doing wonders'; Ps 77:11,14; 78:12; 88:10,12; 89:5 'your wonders'), of the messianic title 'Wonderful Counselor' (Isa 9:6), of God's extraordinary judgments (Isa 25:1; 29:14 'wonder upon wonder'), of the splendor of divine testimonies (Ps 119:129 'your testimonies are wonderful'), of extraordinary visions (Dan 12:6 'the wonders'), and of unusual, astonishing events (Lam 1:9). Multilingual glosses confirm the semantic unity: Arabic 'ajab/aja'ib' (wonder/wonders), German 'Wunder', Korean 'giihan il' (extraordinary deed), Spanish 'maravilla'. All forms (absolute, construct with suffixes, plural) represent a single concept of that which inspires awe at its extraordinary, often divine, character.
